text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a software development practice where team members regularly merge their code changes into a shared repository. The key to this process is automation. Every time a developer submits new code, a CI pipeline automatically triggers a build. This means the software is compiled from the latest code to ensure everything works together. Following the build, the pipeline runs a suite of automated tests. These tests check for bugs, performance issues, and security vulnerabilities. By running these checks continuously, CI allows teams to catch issues early, often within minutes of the change. This prevents small problems from becoming large, complex errors later, making the development process faster and more reliable.
